hypotheses.reasoning: At 20:22:57Z payment-svc reloaded CARDPROC_API_KEY from the secrets store as version 18 and revoked version 17 (#965). Charges succeeded for about 90 seconds after that, then from 20:24:24Z payment-svc began getting 401 invalid_api_key from the card processor (#1046, #1113, #1149). This means the service is still presenting the revoked key 17 (stale key cache or a partial reload), not the new key 18. The 401s propagate: order-service gets 502 from payment-svc (#1164, #1343), order-service returns 502 to api-gateway, and the gateway returns 502 on POST /checkout (#1091, #1208, #1290, #1392), which is the alert. webhook-dispatcher 502s are a separate customer-side problem and are not the cause. The card processor could be rejecting keys on its side, but the 401 starts right after the local key rotation at #965, so an external cause is unlikely.

verdict.recommendedAction: Make payment-svc load the current CARDPROC_API_KEY (version 18): force a secrets reload or restart the instances so none still hold the revoked version 17. Confirm that card-processor calls return 200 again, then watch the POST /checkout 502 rate drop. Going forward, do not revoke the old key until all instances have confirmed the new version. Also check the webhook-dispatcher 502s separately.
